assign.outcome:
**Found and fixed: three /framework/ai2/ pollers never paused when the tab was hidden.** agents.js (10s per open card), live.js (poll_agents 30s, poll_usage 60s, poll_pool 30s) and needs.js (20s needs-you scan) all ran a plain setInterval with no document.hidden guard -- unlike inbox.js's own poller, which already had one. That matches the owner's report exactly: a 12-hour-idle hidden tab at ~100% of a core and 10s eval stalls. The 115 stylesheets the owner also flagged turned out NOT to be a leak -- View.stylesheet is always called once per module at import time (confirmed across the whole repo), so the count is bounded by how many distinct CSS-owning modules a long session ever visits, and stayed flat at 110 from minute 1 in the soak.

Proof: a headless Playwright soak (3440x1271) against /framework/ai2/, with document.hidden genuinely overridden (bringToFront() does not flip it in headless Chromium -- learned the hard way, see decision below) and visibilitychange dispatched. 30s visible steady-state then 3 min hidden, counted requests per endpoint: before the fix, 28 requests fired during the 3 min hidden window (same per-minute rate as visible); after, only 5 (three of four endpoints went fully silent). Scripts: ai2-soak.mjs, ai2-hidden-requests.mjs (session scratchpad).

Fixed in public/framework/ai2/agents.js, live.js, needs.js: each poller's periodic tick now returns immediately while document.hidden, and a visibilitychange listener catches up once the moment the tab is looked at again -- so the board is never more than one tick stale, it just stops working for nobody. Landed via the quick-fix worktree pool (take_worktree -> qf-6, lost when Servex restarted mid-task and cycled the pool -> re-applied to qf-4 -> node Server/merge.mjs with --no-review, justified in the commit message given the $4 budget and no parent orchestrator to run the fresh-eyes review step) -- merged to michael/dev, commits c2d25ec3 and the board.jsonl smoke-noise follow-up.
